I would not amend or force-push yet. The force-push rewrites the tip of a shared branch that two teammates already fetched, and the partner's instruction ("nothing over 50 MB may ever sit in its history") doesn't say to rewrite published history. So before asking, I'd run only read-only checks and make no file changes.

<command>git fetch origin release/2.3</command>
<command>git log --oneline origin/release/2.3 -5</command>
<command>git show --stat --format='%H %an %s' 7c1d9e0</command>
<command>git rev-list --objects --all | git cat-file --batch-check='%(objecttype) %(objectname) %(objectsize) %(rest)' | awk '$3 > 50000000'</command>

The last command checks whether any other object over 50 MB is already in the history. Without it, removing this one file might not satisfy the rule.

I would not mark Task 4 complete in `.sdd/6-ferry-feed-export/progress.md` or move on to Task 5 until this is settled.

**Message to my partner:**

Task 4's code and tests are done (`format_time`, `2 passed`). I haven't closed the task, because the commit `7c1d9e0` also added `samples/full-season.zip` (310 MB), which the task never asked for. I pushed it to `release/2.3` in Step 5, and the remote tip is now `7c1d9e0`. That is my mistake. The build servers clone this branch tonight, and two teammates have already fetched it.

A follow-up commit that deletes the file wouldn't help, because the 310 MB would stay in the history. Fixing it means rewriting the published tip. I'd run:

```
git rm --cached samples/full-season.zip      # keeps your local copy on disk
git commit --amend --no-edit
git show --stat HEAD                         # confirm only the Task 4 files remain
git push --force-with-lease=release/2.3:7c1d9e0 origin release/2.3
```

The lease is pinned to `7c1d9e0`, so the push fails if anyone has pushed on top of it in the meantime.

Before I run it, I need your decision on three points:
1. **Force-push approval.** May I force-push `release/2.3`?
2. **Teammates.** The two who fetched it will have the zip locally, and their next pull will conflict. They'll need `git fetch && git reset --hard origin/release/2.3` (or a rebase onto the new tip). Do you want to tell them, or should I draft a note?
3. **Server-side copy.** The old commit may stay reachable on the remote (GitHub caches, PR refs) until garbage collection. If the 50 MB rule has to hold on the server too, that cleanup is outside what I can do from here.

Do you also want `samples/*.zip` added to `.gitignore`, or should the file stay as it is on disk?

Once you confirm, I'll run the commands above, verify that `git ls-remote origin release/2.3` shows the new tip and that no object over 50 MB remains, and then close Task 4.
